subject: maths
title: Year 4 Time: am, pm and How Long
seo_title: Year 4 Time Worksheets: am and pm, Units of Time, Duration and Calendars (Free, with Answer Key)
standard_text: Solve problems involving the duration of time including situations involving “am” and “pm” and conversions between units of time
meta_desc: Free Year 4 maths worksheets on time for the Australian Curriculum (AC9M4M03): read analog clocks to the minute with am and pm, convert hours, minutes and seconds, work out how long events last across midday, count days on a calendar and solve timetable problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: An hour has 60 minutes, not 100. Count on in jumps through midday.
key_sub: am is midnight to midday, pm is midday to midnight, and midday is 12:00 pm. 2½ hours = 150 minutes. From 4 March to 19 March is 19 − 4 = 15 days: do not count the start day.
body_html:
am and pm

A day has 24 hours. An analog clock goes around twice. am times go from midnight to midday (night and morning). pm times go from midday to midnight (afternoon and evening).

Midday is 12:00 pm and midnight is 12:00 am. One minute after 11:59 am, the time becomes 12:00 pm.

Units of time

UnitEquals
1 minute60 seconds
1 hour60 minutes
1 day24 hours
1 week7 days
1 fortnight14 days
1 year12 months
1 year365 days (366 in a leap year)
Hours to minutes

212 hours = ? minutes

2 hours = 2 × 60 = 120 minutes. Half an hour = 30 minutes. 120 + 30 = 150.

Answer: 150 minutes

Minutes to hours

200 minutes = ? hours and minutes

3 × 60 = 180, and 200 − 180 = 20.

Answer: 3 hours 20 minutes

How long? Count on in jumps

An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers. Jump to the next o’clock, then on in whole hours (through midday), then to the end time.

Finding the end time

A movie starts at 11:50 am and lasts 1 hour 50 minutes. When does it end?

11:50 am + 1 hour = 12:50 pm. + 10 minutes = 1:00 pm. + 40 minutes = 1:40 pm.

Answer: 1:40 pm

Days between dates

To find how many days from one date to another in the same month, subtract the dates. Do not count the start day: no time has passed yet on that day.

On a calendar

How many days is it from 4 March to 19 March?

19 − 4 = 15. Count the jumps: 5, 6 … 19.

Answer: 15 days

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
9:40 am to 11:15 am worked out as 1115 − 940 = 1 hour 75 minutesCount on: 20 minutes + 1 hour + 15 minutes = 1 hour 35 minutes
212 hours written as 250 minutes or 2 hours 50 minutesHalf an hour is 30 minutes: 120 + 30 = 150 minutes
20 minutes after 11:50 am written as 12:10 amAfter midday the time is pm: 12:10 pm
Midday written as 12:00 amMidday is 12:00 pm. Midnight is 12:00 am
4 March to 19 March counted as 16 daysDo not count the start day: 19 − 4 = 15 days

faq.q: What do Year 4 students learn about time in Australia?
faq.a: In the Australian Curriculum v9.0 (AC9M4M03), Year 4 students solve problems about how long things last, including times that go from am to pm, and convert between units of time such as hours, minutes and seconds.
12:00 pm is midday (noon) and 12:00 am is midnight. One minute after 11:59 am is 12:00 pm, so lunch at 12:30 is 12:30 pm.

faq.q: How do you work out how long something lasts across midday?
faq.a: Count on in jumps: to the next o’clock, then whole hours through 12:00 pm, then the extra minutes. For 9:40 am to 1:15 pm that is 20 minutes + 3 hours + 15 minutes = 3 hours 35 minutes.

faq.q: Do you count the first day when working out days between dates?
faq.a: No. From 4 March to 19 March is 19 − 4 = 15 days. Only count both days when you want the number of days an event is on, such as a camp from Monday to Friday (5 days).

sets.title: Read analog clocks to the minute and write am or pm

items.q: What is midday (noon) in 12-hour time?
items.e: Midday is 12 o’clock in the middle of the day. Times from midday to midnight are pm, so midday is 12:00 pm. 12:00 am is midnight.

The short hour hand is between 6 and 7, so the hour is still 6. The long minute hand points to 9. Count in 5s: 9 × 5 = 45 minutes past. It is the morning, before midday, so it is am. So it is 6:45 am.

The short hour hand is between 8 and 9, so the hour is still 8. The long minute hand points to 2. Count in 5s: 2 × 5 = 10 minutes past. It is the morning, before midday, so it is am. So it is 8:10 am.

The short hour hand is between 11 and 12, so the hour is still 11. The long minute hand points to 4. Count in 5s: 4 × 5 = 20 minutes past. It is the morning, before midday, so it is am. So it is 11:20 am.

items.q: It is 5 minutes after midnight. What time is it?
items.e: A new day starts at midnight, and times from midnight to midday are am. So 5 minutes after midnight is 12:05 am. (11:55 pm is 5 minutes before midnight.)

The short hour hand is between 7 and 8, so the hour is still 7. The long minute hand is 3 small marks past the 10. Count in 5s to 50, then on in 1s: 53 minutes past. It is the morning, before midday, so it is am. So it is 7:53 am.

At 7:48 the long hand is 3 small marks past the 9 (count in 5s to 45, then on in 1s to 48), and the short hand is between 7 and 8. That is clock C. (Clock A shows 8:48; clock B shows 7:12; clock D shows 7:09.)

The short hour hand is between 12 and 1, so the hour is still 12. The long minute hand is 2 small marks past the 9. Count in 5s to 45, then on in 1s: 47 minutes past. The hour is 12 and it is just after midday, so it is pm (not am). So it is 12:47 pm.

items.q: It is 11:50 am. What time will it be in 20 minutes?
items.e: 11:50 am + 10 minutes = 12:00 pm (midday). 10 more minutes makes 12:10. It is now after midday, so the time changes from am to pm: 12:10 pm.

The short hour hand is between 2 and 3, so the hour is still 2. The long minute hand is 3 small marks past the 1. Count in 5s to 5, then on in 1s: 8 minutes past. It is after midday, so it is pm. So it is 2:08 pm.

The short hour hand is between 3 and 4, so the hour is still 3. The long minute hand is 4 small marks past the 9. Count in 5s to 45, then on in 1s: 49 minutes past. It is after midday, so it is pm. So it is 3:49 pm.

items.q: Write 13 minutes to 7 in the evening as a digital time with am or pm.
items.e: “13 minutes to 7” means 13 minutes before 7 o’clock. 60 − 13 = 47, so it is 47 minutes past 6. It is in the evening, so it is pm: 6:47 pm.

The short hour hand is between 5 and 6, so the hour is still 5. The long minute hand is 4 small marks past the 3. Count in 5s to 15, then on in 1s: 19 minutes past. It is after midday, so it is pm. So it is 5:19 pm.

At 4:13 the long hand is 3 small marks past the 2 (count in 5s to 10, then on in 1s to 13), and the short hand is between 4 and 5. That is clock B. (Clock A shows 5:13; clock C shows 4:47; clock D shows 4:02.)

items.q: It is 12:10 pm. What time was it 15 minutes ago?
items.e: Count back 10 minutes to 12:00 pm (midday), then 5 more minutes to 11:55. That is before midday, so it is 11:55 am. (12:25 pm is 15 minutes later, not earlier.)

The short hour hand is between 6 and 7, so the hour is still 6. The long minute hand is 1 small mark past the 7. Count in 5s to 35, then on in 1s: 36 minutes past. It is after midday, so it is pm. So it is 6:36 pm.

items.q: Write quarter to 1 in the afternoon as a digital time with am or pm.
items.e: “quarter to 1” means 15 minutes before 1 o’clock. 60 − 15 = 45, so it is 45 minutes past 12. It is in the afternoon, so it is pm: 12:45 pm. (Quarter to 1 is still in the 12 o’clock hour, and after midday is pm.)

The short hour hand is between 8 and 9, so the hour is still 8. The long minute hand is 2 small marks past the 5. Count in 5s to 25, then on in 1s: 27 minutes past. It is after midday, so it is pm. So it is 8:27 pm.

items.q: Write 22 minutes past 11 at night as a digital time with am or pm.
items.e: “22 minutes past 11” means 22 minutes after 11 o’clock. It is at night, so it is pm: 11:22 pm.

items.q: Write 8 minutes to 12 just before midday as a digital time with am or pm.
items.e: “8 minutes to 12” means 8 minutes before 12 o’clock. 60 − 8 = 52, so it is 52 minutes past 11. It is just before midday, so it is am: 11:52 am. (Not 12:52 pm: the time is before 12 o’clock, and before midday is am.)

sets.title: Units of time and converting between them

items.q: How many seconds are in 1 minute?
items.e: There are 60 seconds in 1 minute. Time does not count in hundreds.

items.q: How many minutes are in 1 hour?
items.e: There are 60 minutes in 1 hour. (Not 100: an hour is not like a dollar with 100 cents.)

items.q: How many hours are in 1 day?
items.e: There are 24 hours in 1 day: 12 am hours (midnight to midday) and 12 pm hours (midday to midnight).

items.q: How many months are in 1 year?
items.e: January to December: 12 months. (52 is about the number of weeks, and 365 is the number of days.)

items.q: How many days are in a year that is not a leap year?
items.e: A normal year has 365 days. A leap year has one extra day (29 February), so it has 366 days.

items.q: How many days are in a leap year?
items.e: A leap year has an extra day, 29 February. 365 + 1 = 366 days. Leap years come every 4 years.

items.q: 3 weeks = ? days
items.e: 1 week = 7 days. 3 × 7 = 21 days. (15 is only the school days in 3 weeks.)

items.q: 3 minutes = ? seconds
items.e: 1 minute = 60 seconds. 3 × 60 = 180 seconds. (Not 300: a minute is 60 seconds, not 100.)

items.q: 4 hours = ? minutes
items.e: 1 hour = 60 minutes. 4 × 60 = 240 minutes. (Not 400: an hour is 60 minutes, not 100.)

items.q: 2 years = ? months
items.e: 1 year = 12 months. 2 × 12 = 24 months. (104 is the number of weeks in 2 years.)

items.q: 34 of an hour = ? minutes
items.e: A quarter of an hour is 60 ÷ 4 = 15 minutes. Three quarters is 3 × 15 = 45 minutes. (75 would be three quarters of 100.)

items.q: 112 minutes = ? seconds
items.e: 1 minute = 60 seconds and half a minute = 30 seconds. 60 + 30 = 90 seconds. (110 comes from reading 112 as 1 minute 50 seconds.)

items.q: 212 hours = ? minutes
items.e: 2 hours = 2 × 60 = 120 minutes. Half an hour = 30 minutes. 120 + 30 = 150 minutes. (170 comes from reading 212 hours as 2 hours 50 minutes.)

items.q: 3 days = ? hours
items.e: 1 day = 24 hours. 3 × 24 = 72 hours. (36 uses 12 hours for a day, but a day is 24 hours.)

items.q: 14 of a day = ? hours
items.e: 1 day = 24 hours. A quarter is 24 ÷ 4 = 6 hours. (15 is a quarter of an hour in minutes, and 12 hours is half a day.)

items.q: 150 minutes = ?
items.e: 60 minutes make 1 hour. 150 = 60 + 60 + 30, so it is 2 hours 30 minutes. (1 hour 50 minutes uses 100 minutes in an hour.)

items.q: 200 seconds = ?
items.e: 60 seconds make 1 minute. 3 × 60 = 180, and 200 − 180 = 20. So it is 3 minutes 20 seconds. (2 minutes uses 100 seconds in a minute.)

items.q: 96 hours = ? days
items.e: 1 day = 24 hours. 24 × 4 = 96, so 96 hours = 4 days. (8 days would use 12 hours for a day.)

items.q: Which time is the longest?
items.e: Change them all to minutes: 112 hours = 90 minutes, 1 hour 35 minutes = 95 minutes, 1 hour 20 minutes = 80 minutes. 100 minutes is the longest (it is 1 hour 40 minutes).

items.q: Which of these is true?
items.e: 1 hour = 60 minutes. 100 − 60 = 40, so 100 minutes = 1 hour 40 minutes. 1 hour 40 minutes = 60 + 40 = 100 minutes, not 140.

sets.title: How long? Durations across am and pm

items.q: Harper starts a maths test at 9:15 am and finishes at 9:52 am. How long does she take?
items.e: Count on: 9:15 am to 9:52 am is 37 minutes. So it is 37 minutes.

items.q: A TV program starts at 2:35 pm and ends at 3:10 pm. How long is it?
items.e: Count on: 2:35 pm to 3:00 pm is 25 minutes, 3:00 pm to 3:10 pm is 10 minutes. 25 minutes + 10 minutes = 35 minutes. (Not 75 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100.)

items.q: Chloe leaves home at 7:40 am and gets to school at 8:25 am. How long is the trip?
items.e: Count on: 7:40 am to 8:00 am is 20 minutes, 8:00 am to 8:25 am is 25 minutes. 20 minutes + 25 minutes = 45 minutes. (Not 85 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100.)

items.q: A school concert goes from 10:20 am to 11:45 am. How long is the concert?
items.e: Count on: 10:20 am to 11:00 am is 40 minutes, 11:00 am to 11:45 am is 45 minutes. 40 minutes + 45 minutes = 1 hour 25 minutes.

items.q: The sausage sizzle cooks from 11:48 am to 12:17 pm. How long is that?
items.e: Count on: 11:48 am to 12:00 pm is 12 minutes, 12:00 pm to 12:17 pm is 17 minutes. 12 minutes + 17 minutes = 29 minutes. (The time goes past midday, so am changes to pm. Count on through 12:00 pm.) (Not 69 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100.)

items.q: Cricket practice goes from 3:45 pm to 5:20 pm. How long is practice?
items.e: Count on: 3:45 pm to 4:00 pm is 15 minutes, 4:00 pm to 5:00 pm is 1 hour, 5:00 pm to 5:20 pm is 20 minutes. 1 hour + 15 minutes + 20 minutes = 1 hour 35 minutes. (Not 1 hour 75 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100.)

items.q: Matilda’s family has dinner at a restaurant from 6:50 pm to 8:05 pm. How long are they there?
items.e: Count on: 6:50 pm to 7:00 pm is 10 minutes, 7:00 pm to 8:00 pm is 1 hour, 8:00 pm to 8:05 pm is 5 minutes. 1 hour + 10 minutes + 5 minutes = 1 hour 15 minutes.

items.q: A cake goes in the oven at 11:30 am and comes out at 12:15 pm. How long does it bake?
items.e: Count on: 11:30 am to 12:00 pm is 30 minutes, 12:00 pm to 12:15 pm is 15 minutes. 30 minutes + 15 minutes = 45 minutes. (The time goes past midday, so am changes to pm. Count on through 12:00 pm.) (Not 85 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100.)

items.q: A movie starts at 10:40 am. It lasts 1 hour 35 minutes. What time does it end?
items.e: 10:40 am + 1 hour = 11:40 am. Then 20 minutes takes it to 12:00 pm (midday), and 15 more minutes makes 12:15 pm. It is after midday, so it is pm. (11:15 am forgets to carry the 60 minutes into the next hour.)

items.q: Kai starts a jigsaw puzzle at 11:25 am and works on it for 50 minutes. What time does he stop?
items.e: 11:25 am + 35 minutes = 12:00 pm (midday). 50 − 35 = 15 more minutes: 12:15 pm. After midday it is pm, not am.

items.q: A school excursion leaves at 10:45 am and gets back at 1:10 pm. How long is it?
items.e: Count on: 10:45 am to 11:00 am is 15 minutes, 11:00 am to 12:00 pm is 1 hour, 12:00 pm to 1:00 pm is 1 hour, 1:00 pm to 1:10 pm is 10 minutes. 1 hour + 1 hour + 15 minutes + 10 minutes = 2 hours 25 minutes. (The time goes past midday, so am changes to pm. Count on through 12:00 pm.) (Not 2 hours 65 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100.)

items.q: The swimming carnival starts at 9:40 am and ends at 1:15 pm. How long does it go for?
items.e: Count on: 9:40 am to 10:00 am is 20 minutes, 10:00 am to 12:00 pm is 2 hours, 12:00 pm to 1:00 pm is 1 hour, 1:00 pm to 1:15 pm is 15 minutes. 2 hours + 1 hour + 20 minutes + 15 minutes = 3 hours 35 minutes. (The time goes past midday, so am changes to pm. Count on through 12:00 pm.) (Not 3 hours 75 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100.)

items.q: Mia’s birthday party goes from 11:20 am to 2:05 pm. How long is the party?
items.e: Count on: 11:20 am to 12:00 pm is 40 minutes, 12:00 pm to 2:00 pm is 2 hours, 2:00 pm to 2:05 pm is 5 minutes. 2 hours + 40 minutes + 5 minutes = 2 hours 45 minutes. (The time goes past midday, so am changes to pm. Count on through 12:00 pm.) (Not 2 hours 85 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100.)

items.q: Ruby must be at the station at 12:10 pm. The walk takes 25 minutes. What is the latest time she can leave home?
items.e: Count back 10 minutes to 12:00 pm (midday), then 15 more: 11:45. It is before midday, so 11:45 am. (12:35 pm counts on instead of back, and 11:35 am forgets the 10 minutes after midday.)

items.q: A bushwalk starts at 9:50 am and takes 2 hours 45 minutes. What time does it finish?
items.e: 9:50 am + 2 hours = 11:50 am. 10 more minutes is 12:00 pm, then 35 more minutes: 12:35 pm. (45 − 10 = 35.)

items.q: The school fete opens at 8:25 am and closes at 12:40 pm. How long is it open?
items.e: Count on: 8:25 am to 9:00 am is 35 minutes, 9:00 am to 12:00 pm is 3 hours, 12:00 pm to 12:40 pm is 40 minutes. 3 hours + 35 minutes + 40 minutes = 4 hours 15 minutes. (The time goes past midday, so am changes to pm. Count on through 12:00 pm.)

items.q: A netball carnival ends at 1:20 pm. It lasted 1 hour 45 minutes. What time did it start?
items.e: Count back 1 hour: 1:20 pm → 12:20 pm. Then back 20 minutes to 12:00 pm and 25 more to 11:35. That is before midday, so it started at 11:35 am. (3:05 pm counts on instead of back.)

items.q: A family drives from Brisbane to the beach. They leave at 10:55 am and arrive at 4:30 pm, after stopping for lunch. How long does the trip take?
items.e: Count on: 10:55 am to 11:00 am is 5 minutes, 11:00 am to 12:00 pm is 1 hour, 12:00 pm to 4:00 pm is 4 hours, 4:00 pm to 4:30 pm is 30 minutes. 1 hour + 4 hours + 5 minutes + 30 minutes = 5 hours 35 minutes. (The time goes past midday, so am changes to pm. Count on through 12:00 pm.) (Not 5 hours 75 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100.)

items.q: A footy match finishes at 4:05 pm. It lasted 2 hours 30 minutes. What time did it start?
items.e: Count back 2 hours: 4:05 pm → 2:05 pm. Then back 30 minutes: 5 minutes to 2:00 pm and 25 more to 1:35 pm. (2:05 pm only takes away the 2 hours.)

items.q: A plane leaves Perth at 10:30 pm and lands in Adelaide at 1:15 am the next morning, Perth time. How long is the flight?
items.e: Count on: 10:30 pm to 11:00 pm is 30 minutes, 11:00 pm to 12:00 am is 1 hour, 12:00 am to 1:00 am is 1 hour, 1:00 am to 1:15 am is 15 minutes. 1 hour + 1 hour + 30 minutes + 15 minutes = 2 hours 45 minutes. (Not 2 hours 85 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100.)

items.q: How many days are in April?
items.e: “30 days has September, April, June and November.” So April has 30 days.

items.q: Which month has 31 days?
items.e: September, April, June and November have 30 days. February has 28 (29 in a leap year). All the others, including July, have 31.

items.q: Look at the calendar. What day of the week is 18 March?
items.e: Find 18 in the calendar and go up its column to the top: Thursday.

items.q: Which year is a leap year?
items.e: Leap years come every 4 years. 2024 was a leap year, so the next one is 2024 + 4 = 2028. (2028 ÷ 4 = 507 with no remainder.)

items.q: 2028 is a leap year. How many days are in February 2028?
items.e: February has 28 days, but in a leap year it gets one extra day: 29 days.

items.q: What is the date of the second Saturday in March 2027?
items.e: The Saturdays are 6, 13, 20, 27. The second one is 13 March. (6 March is the first Saturday and 14 March is a Sunday.)

items.q: Ava has a swimming lesson every Friday in March. How many lessons is that?
items.e: The Fridays are 5, 12, 19, 26. That is 4 lessons. (Not every month has 5 of each day.)

items.q: What is the date 1 week after Thursday 11 March?
items.e: 1 week = 7 days. 11 + 7 = 18. Go straight down one row on the calendar: Thursday 18 March. (17 March counts 11 March as the first day.)

items.q: What is the date 10 days after 12 March?
items.e: 12 + 10 = 22 March. (21 March counts 12 March as one of the 10 days.)

items.q: How many days is it from 4 March to 19 March?
items.e: 19 − 4 = 15 days. Count the jumps from one day to the next: 5, 6, 7 … 19 is 15 jumps. (16 counts 4 March as well, but no time has passed on the start day.)

items.q: What day of the week will 1 April 2027 be?
items.e: 31 March is a Wednesday, and 1 April is the next day, so it is a Thursday. (A new month does not start on a new row: it carries on from the last day of March.)

items.q: Today is 21 March. Zara’s birthday is on 30 March. How many days until her birthday?
items.e: 30 − 21 = 9 days. (10 counts today as one of the days.)

items.q: Today is 9 March. The school excursion is on 26 March. How many days until the excursion?
items.e: 26 − 9 = 17 days. (18 counts today as well.)

items.q: Liam borrows a library book on 3 March. It is due back 2 weeks later. What is the due date?
items.e: 2 weeks = 14 days. 3 + 14 = 17 March. On the calendar, go down 2 rows from 3. (10 March is only 1 week later, and 5 March adds 2 days, not 2 weeks.)

items.q: What is the date 3 weeks after 5 March?
items.e: 3 weeks = 3 × 7 = 21 days. 5 + 21 = 26 March. On the calendar, go down 3 rows from 5. (19 March is only 2 weeks later.)

items.q: Today is 14 June. What will the date be in 9 days?
items.e: 14 + 9 = 23 June. (22 June counts today as one of the 9 days, and 5 June counts back.)

items.q: Lachlan stays with his grandparents from Saturday 6 March to Saturday 27 March. How many weeks is that?
items.e: 27 − 6 = 21 days. 21 ÷ 7 = 3 weeks. On the calendar, 27 is 3 rows below 6. (4 weeks counts the rows from 6 to 27 instead of the jumps.)

items.q: School camp starts on Monday 15 March and ends on Friday 19 March. On how many days is the camp, counting both Monday and Friday?
items.e: The camp is on Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday: 5 days. Here we count the days the camp is on, so both the first and last day count. (19 − 15 = 4 is the number of nights.)

items.q: How many days is it from 1 May to 31 May?
items.e: 31 − 1 = 30 days. May has 31 dates, but from the 1st to the 31st there are 30 jumps. (31 counts 1 May as well.)

items.q: Year 4 camp leaves on 8 August and comes home on 12 August. How many nights are the students away?
items.e: Nights away: 8th, 9th, 10th and 11th. 12 − 8 = 4 nights. (5 counts the days the camp is on, not the nights.)

sets.title: Timetables and everyday problems: school, swimming and movies

items.q: Look at the timetable. How long is recess?
items.e: Count on: 10:50 am to 11:00 am is 10 minutes, 11:00 am to 11:20 am is 20 minutes. 10 minutes + 20 minutes = 30 minutes. (Not 70 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100.)

items.q: How long is lunch?
items.e: Count on: 1:10 pm to 2:00 pm is 50 minutes. So it is 50 minutes. (Not 90 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100.)

items.q: What time does the Dolphins class finish?
items.e: 4:20 pm + 40 minutes = 5:00 pm. 45 − 40 = 5 more minutes: 5:05 pm. (4:05 pm forgets to carry into the next hour: 20 + 45 = 65 minutes = 1 hour 5 minutes.)

items.q: What time does Koala Rescue end?
items.e: 10:15 am + 1 hour = 11:15 am. 11:15 am + 35 minutes = 11:50 am. It is still before midday, so it is am.

items.q: How long is Session 2?
items.e: Count on: 11:20 am to 12:00 pm is 40 minutes, 12:00 pm to 1:00 pm is 1 hour, 1:00 pm to 1:10 pm is 10 minutes. 1 hour + 40 minutes + 10 minutes = 1 hour 50 minutes. (The time goes past midday, so am changes to pm. Count on through 12:00 pm.) (Not 1 hour 90 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100.)

items.q: Which movie is the longest?
c: They are all the same length.
items.e: Koala Rescue is 95 minutes, Space Kids is 110 minutes and Ocean Quest is 2 × 60 + 5 = 125 minutes. Ocean Quest is the longest.

items.q: Sienna gets to the pool at 4:40 pm and waits for the Sharks class to start. How long does she wait?
items.e: Count on: 4:40 pm to 5:00 pm is 20 minutes, 5:00 pm to 5:15 pm is 15 minutes. 20 minutes + 15 minutes = 35 minutes. (Not 75 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100.)

items.q: How long is the whole school day, from the start of Session 1 to the end of Session 3?
items.e: Count on: 8:50 am to 9:00 am is 10 minutes, 9:00 am to 12:00 pm is 3 hours, 12:00 pm to 3:00 pm is 3 hours, 3:00 pm to 3:10 pm is 10 minutes. 3 hours + 3 hours + 10 minutes + 10 minutes = 6 hours 20 minutes. (The time goes past midday, so am changes to pm. Count on through 12:00 pm.) (Not 6 hours 60 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100.)

items.q: What time does Space Kids end?
items.e: 11:50 am + 1 hour = 12:50 pm. 12:50 pm + 10 minutes = 1:00 pm, then 40 more minutes: 1:40 pm. (12:40 pm forgets to carry: 50 + 50 = 100 minutes = 1 hour 40 minutes.)

items.q: A junior netball game has 4 quarters of 10 minutes with a 3-minute break between quarters. How long is the whole game?
items.e: Playing time: 4 × 10 = 40 minutes. There are 3 breaks between 4 quarters: 3 × 3 = 9 minutes. 40 + 9 = 49 minutes. (52 counts 4 breaks.)

items.q: How many minutes long is Ocean Quest?
items.e: 2 hours = 2 × 60 = 120 minutes. 120 + 5 = 125 minutes. (205 uses 100 minutes in an hour.)

items.q: Amelia goes to the Sharks class once a week for 4 weeks. How much time is that in the pool?
items.e: 4 × 50 = 200 minutes. 200 = 60 + 60 + 60 + 20, so it is 3 hours 20 minutes. (2 hours uses 100 minutes in an hour.)

items.q: Charlotte puts a lasagne in the oven at 5:35 pm. It cooks for 114 hours. What time will it be ready?
items.e: 114 hours = 1 hour 15 minutes. 5:35 pm + 1 hour = 6:35 pm. 6:35 pm + 15 minutes = 6:50 pm. (7:00 pm reads 114 hours as 1 hour 25 minutes, and 6:00 pm adds only 25 minutes.)

items.q: How much time is spent in the three sessions altogether?
items.e: Session 1: 2 hours. Session 2: 1 hour 50 minutes. Session 3: 1 hour 10 minutes. 2 hours + 1 hour 50 minutes + 1 hour 10 minutes = 4 hours 60 minutes = 5 hours. (6 hours 20 minutes is the whole day, with recess and lunch.)

items.q: A term of Starfish lessons has 9 classes. How long is that altogether?
items.e: 9 × 30 = 270 minutes. 270 = 4 × 60 + 30, so it is 4 hours 30 minutes. (2 hours 70 minutes uses 100 minutes in an hour, and 27 hours mixes up minutes and hours.)

items.q: Before Ocean Quest there are 15 minutes of ads. The movie starts after the ads. What time does the movie end?
items.e: The movie starts at 4:40 pm + 15 minutes = 4:55 pm. 4:55 pm + 2 hours = 6:55 pm. 6:55 pm + 5 minutes = 7:00 pm. (6:45 pm forgets the ads.)

items.q: A family leaves Sydney at 10:30 am and drives to Canberra. They drive for 3 hours and stop for lunch for 25 minutes. What time do they arrive?
items.e: 10:30 am + 3 hours = 1:30 pm (11:30, 12:30, 1:30). Add the 25-minute stop: 1:55 pm. After midday it is pm. (1:30 pm forgets the lunch stop.)

items.q: A Year 4 excursion bus leaves school at 9:15 am and gets back at 3:45 pm. How long are the students away from school?
items.e: Count on: 9:15 am to 10:00 am is 45 minutes, 10:00 am to 12:00 pm is 2 hours, 12:00 pm to 3:00 pm is 3 hours, 3:00 pm to 3:45 pm is 45 minutes. 2 hours + 3 hours + 45 minutes + 45 minutes = 6 hours 30 minutes. (The time goes past midday, so am changes to pm. Count on through 12:00 pm.)

items.q: Zara reads for 25 minutes every day for a fortnight. How long does she read altogether?
items.e: A fortnight is 14 days. 14 × 25 = 350 minutes. 350 = 5 × 60 + 50, so it is 5 hours 50 minutes. (3 hours 50 minutes uses 100 minutes in an hour, and 2 hours 55 minutes uses only 7 days.)

items.q: Isla’s alarm goes off at 6:45 am. She slept for 1012 hours. What time did she go to sleep the night before?
items.e: 1012 hours = 10 hours 30 minutes. Count back 10 hours from 6:45 am: 8:45 pm the night before. Then back 30 minutes: 8:15 pm. It was in the evening, so it is pm, not am. (5:15 pm counts on instead of back, and 7:55 pm reads 1012 hours as 10 hours 50 minutes.)
